installSteps.text: Alternatively, download UnMech3 directly from the official site at https://unmech3.org/. Always download from the official source — third-party mirrors of free games are a common malware vector.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Open the downloaded .dmg and drag the app into Applications. On first launch macOS may refuse to open it as unidentified — right-click the app and choose Open to approve it once.
Check your distribution's package manager first, which is usually the easiest route. Otherwise download the AppImage from the official site, mark it executable and run it.
Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. UnMech3 needs roughly small of free disk space.

set.tagline: MechWarrior 3 gets a second engine bay, and the old hardware still matters.
set.description: UnMech3 is Sake906's Unity rebuild of MechWarrior 3, focused on preserving its weighty combat and opening the game to new maps and Mechs. The project is free, but it requires an owned, patched MechWarrior 3 installation or its original ZBD data. Windows and Linux builds are available; multiplayer uses the project's own servers.
set.license: Free fan project; original MechWarrior 3 assets required

systemRequirements.min: Windows or Linux; original MechWarrior 3 data (the ZBD folder) from a lawful copy, with the original game updated to v1.2. The UnMech3 developer has not published a numerical CPU, RAM, GPU or installed-storage minimum. Current stable Windows and Linux archives are about 61 MB and 75 MB respectively before extraction and base assets.
systemRequirements.recommended: Windows or Linux with the same owned and patched original game files. Use current graphics drivers and enough free storage for the copied base assets plus the extracted rebuild; no numerical recommended PC specification has been published by the developer.

min.notes: Requires an owned MechWarrior 3 installation or its original ZBD assets and the official v1.2 game patch. The developer has not published numerical CPU, RAM, GPU or installed-space minimums. Stable archives alone are about 61 MB for Windows and 75 MB for Linux.

recommended.notes: Use current graphics drivers and leave room for the original game files and extracted rebuild. No numerical recommended CPU, RAM, GPU or storage target is published.

qualityBar.verdict: Every ton in the MechBay feels like a choice you will have to defend once the shooting starts.

set.longDescription:
UnMech3 begins with a problem familiar to anyone who still cares about MechWarrior 3: a great giant-robot game is trapped inside the machinery of a 1999 PC release. Sake906's answer is to rebuild its play space in Unity while reading the original game's assets, rather than pretending those assets are theirs to give away. It is a fan project with a real dependency. You need a lawful copy of MechWarrior 3, its original ZBD data and the official v1.2 patch before the new executable has anything meaningful to load. That is an awkward first step, but it is also the honest one.

The attraction is the relationship between the machine you assemble and the machine you take into a fight. MechWarrior 3 treated movement, mass and weapon choices as things with consequences. A BattleMech is not a character skin that happens to fire missiles; its engine, armor and hardpoints define how it crosses a map and what it can survive there. The rebuild's MechBay keeps that tinkering in view. Its creator has shown work on new Mechs and tools for building more, alongside the original designs. A screenshot from the creator's ModDB page shows a Catapult surrounded by supply lists, component slots and a rather serious set of decisions about what belongs inside the chassis.

This is still a developing rebuild, not a complete modern replacement for the original release. The creator's stated aims include easier matchmaking, co-op missions, additional content and modding tools. Some are ambitions rather than features we can promise today. The project's updater history does confirm Windows and Linux clients and a Linux game server, so multiplayer exists beyond a design document. PlayBound has not yet verified its server protocol, player cap, controller mapping or an automatic party join, and it has no tested VPS recipe for this game. Those edges matter if your first goal is to invite friends and be playing immediately.

Installation deserves the same candor. The developer offers Windows and Linux stable ZIPs and updater scripts. Both approaches expect you to start from your own MechWarrior 3 files; a downloaded ZIP alone is not a complete game. There is no current macOS build listed, despite what this Draft previously claimed. The published requirements explain the original-data dependency but do not give numerical modern CPU, memory or GPU targets, so we will not dress a guess up as a hardware specification.

We like projects that make an old game easier to inhabit without erasing what made it distinctive. UnMech3's best idea is not just a cleaner route into a cockpit. It is preserving a particular kind of heavy, technical combat while giving its community room to build on it. That promise is worth following, and the ownership and setup work should be visible before anyone clicks Install.
set.whyWePickedIt: We picked UnMech3 because its creator is rebuilding the weight and customization of MechWarrior 3 for a community that still plays it, while making new Mechs, maps and multiplayer possible. The owned-base-game requirement and PlayBound integration gaps remain explicit during testing.
set.thatOneThing: In the MechBay, replacing an engine changes more than a number: it changes what the entire walking arsenal can carry into the fight.

installSteps.text: Use an owned copy of MechWarrior 3. Keep its original ZBD asset folder and update the base game to the official v1.2 patch before installing UnMech3; the fan project cannot supply those copyrighted files.

From unmech3.org, download the stable Windows ZIP or the UnMechUpdater2.bat script. Place it in the root of your MechWarrior 3 installation and extract the ZIP or run the developer's updater. The resulting UnMech3 folder contains the game's executable. PlayBound currently opens the official site for this owned-assets install.

From unmech3.org, download the stable Linux ZIP or UnMechUpdater2.sh. Supply your own original MechWarrior 3 ZBD data and follow the developer's placement instructions. The website does not publish a macOS build. PlayBound currently opens the official site rather than claiming an automatic Linux install.

firstPlaySteps.text: Confirm the original ZBD assets are present before launching UnMech3. Open the MechBay to inspect a chassis, engine, armor and weapon loadout, then check the game's current controls and server browser. PlayBound controller behavior has not been verified.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Use UnMech3's own online server flow after installing the same current build as your friends. The developer documents a Linux game server, but PlayBound has not verified an automatic party connection or provisioned a VPS server recipe for this Draft.

faq.a: The fan project is free, but it cannot run without MechWarrior 3 game assets from a copy you own. PlayBound does not distribute those assets.
The developer publishes stable Windows and Linux archives and updater scripts. No current macOS build is listed.

faq.q: Can I install it with one click in PlayBound?
faq.a: Not yet. The current PlayBound entry opens the developer's download page because the install must combine UnMech3 with your original MechWarrior 3 assets.
The project has Windows and Linux clients and a Linux game server. PlayBound has not yet tested automatic party joining, a player cap or VPS hosting for it.
No controller mapping has been verified for the current build. PlayBound will not label it controller-supported until one is tested.

The developer documents the original-data dependency, but does not publish numerical modern CPU, memory, graphics or installed-storage requirements. The stable downloads themselves are about 61 MB on Windows and 75 MB on Linux.

bestFor: MechWarrior 3 owners who miss its heavy movement and technical loadouts
Pilots interested in community Mechs, maps and online battles
notFor: Players without an owned copy of MechWarrior 3 and its original assets
Anyone expecting verified one-click installation or PlayBound-hosted servers today
